newsitem.title: UK: NatWest shares defy UK market gloom.
newsitem.headline: NatWest shares defy UK market gloom.

text.p: Shares in National Westminster Bank Plc stood out against the gloomy tone gripping UK equities on Thursday after an early mark-down prompted buying of one of the bank sector's worst performers of 1996, traders and analysts said.
NatWest shares were up 3-1/2p at 689 by 1118 GMT in volume of 3.5 million shares, making it the second most active stock in the FTSE 100 index.
By contrast the FTSE was down 30.2 points at 4,088.3, after earlier dropping as low as 4,067.5 in the wake of a sharp New Year's Eve decline on Wall Street.

"The stock was called sharply lower at the opening but there were some buyers at the lower levels," said one market-maker at a leading brokerage. Ian Poulter, analyst at Williams de Broe, said NatWest was one of the poorest performers among UK banks during 1996 and it was possible some investors were buying it on hopes it would improve on that performance in the coming year.
He said NatWest's above-average dividend yield of 4.8 percent could also make it attractive to some investors.
Poulter said bank stocks as a whole should remain firm, at least until the release of 1996 results in mid February, with continuing hopes of share buybacks and special dividends providing support.
Yet the sector's outlook beyond that point was more mixed, he said, being clouded by political uncertainties and fears of rising interest rates.
"I have a "neutral" position on the sector going into 1997 for the first time in four or five years," Poulter said.

"Potentially it is going to be a pretty good results season, but over the last five years the sector has outperformed quite substantially and you have got to look at what is already in the price. But there are still some good individual stories in there."
Elsewhere in the bank sector Lloyds TSB Plc was up 2-1/2p at 433 in active trade of 1.8 million shares and Bank of Scotland Plc was up 1/2p at 309.
